title: Korean data-protection enforcement datasets: PIPC sanction decisions, fine calculation grounds, KCC decisions, dispute mediation, civil damages judgments and commencement dates
description:
Six tables covering how Korea's personal data laws are enforced, published as plain CSV so they can be cited, checked and reused.

Contents. (1) Sanction decisions published by the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC); (2) administrative fine calculation grounds extracted from the reasoning sections of PIPC decisions; (3) decisions of the now-abolished Korea Communications Commission (KCC) in personal data cases, extracted by OCR from scanned decision PDFs; (4) disputes resolved by the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee; (5) civil judgments awarding or refusing damages for data breaches; (6) Korean statutes and subordinate rules with future commencement dates.

Method. The tables are built by reading the underlying decisions and judgments rather than the press releases. Extraction is programmatic except for a small number of hand-classified columns and one hand-compiled table (civil damages judgments). KCC decisions survive only as scanned PDFs with no text layer and are recovered by OCR, which carries the extra error modes that implies. Each row carries a stable anchor and a link to the original document.

Scope and limits. Only documents the issuing body has actually published are counted. The Commission anonymises many respondents, so any count broken down by company is a lower bound rather than a census. Cases known only from a press release are held separately and their amounts are not added to the totals. Accuracy is not guaranteed; verify against the original document before relying on an individual case.

Documentation. Column headings are in Korean; the README and the source pages carry English documentation. The live tables, which are updated as the collectors run, are at https://datalaw.kr/ .
